query: Which material can be used for ductility, and why?

generation.hypothesis: The eutectic high‐entropy alloy AlCoCrFeNi2.1 exhibits superior ductility because its fine lamellar microstructure (alternating soft fcc and hard B2 phases) promotes efficient dislocation storage and strain hardening, thereby accommodating large plastic deformations.
generation.material_initial_state: As‐cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic high‐entropy alloy with a fine lamellar fcc/B2 microstructure.
generation.intervention: Processing via vacuum induction melting (and optionally cold rolling) to produce the eutectic microstructure.
generation.conditions: Tensile testing at room temperature and elevated temperatures (up to 700°C) under controlled deformation rates.
generation.structural_mediator: The alternating lamellar structure that combines soft, deformable fcc regions with hard, strengthening B2 regions.
generation.mechanism: The soft fcc phase stores dislocations while the hard B2 phase pins them, leading to high strain hardening and delayed onset of necking. This synergistic interaction between phases reduces stress concentrations, thereby enhancing ductility.
generation.predicted_outcome: The alloy should exhibit high fracture strength along with significant ductility (e.g., elongation around 25% or higher), outperforming conventional homogeneous alloys.
generation.baseline: Conventional cast alloys with homogeneous microstructures that typically display lower ductility and strain-hardening capability.
generation.boundary: The beneficial effect is contingent on maintaining a uniformly distributed, fine lamellar microstructure. Any processing variations that coarsen the lamellae or induce segregation may compromise the ductile behavior.
generation.uncertainty: While the lamellar design is promising, the exact processing window and microstructural control required to consistently achieve these ductility levels remain to be precisely defined.

falsification_experiment.design: Fabricate two sets of AlCoCrFeNi2.1 alloy samples: one set processed to achieve the desired fine lamellar fcc/B2 microstructure and a control set with a deliberately coarser, more homogeneous microstructure. Perform standardized tensile tests at room temperature and at elevated temperatures (up to 700°C).
measurements: Microstructural characterization (using SEM/TEM to assess lamellar spacing and phase distribution)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the samples with the fine lamellar architecture do not exhibit significantly higher ductility (i.e., elongation ~25% or greater) compared to the control samples, or if variations in microstructure do not correlate with changes in ductility, the proposed mechanism is refuted.
